{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**Prepared by:** In-house counsel (Customer side)  
**Subject:** Playbook review of the Vendor's Master Services Agreement — verified findings

---

## 1. Executive summary

We reviewed the MSA against the playbook and identified **nine items requiring action** out of eighteen rules assessed. Nine clauses already meet our preferred position and require no redline (limitation of liability, assignment, licence scope, warranties, audit, renewal, insurance, exclusivity and liquidated damages).

The critical exposures are:

- **No indemnity at all.** The Agreement jumps from Section 19 (Warranties) to Section 21 (Limitation of Liability). Several clauses presuppose an indemnity that does not exist (§ 9.3 cross-refers to a "Section 20.5", §§ 19.4/19.5 refer to "indemnified claims" and "indemnity", § 21.3 makes "indemnification obligations" Excluded Claims, § 30.5 preserves "indemnified party" rights). We are inserting a new Section 20 at the preferred level — Vendor defence and indemnity for third-party IP infringement, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused data breach and gross negligence/wilful misconduct — rather than the fallback, because the fallback's 3× annual-fee super-cap would be worse than the existing uncapped treatment of indemnification obligations under § 21.3.
- **Deliverable ownership runs the wrong way.** § 14.2 vests exclusive ownership of every Deliverable created for us in Vendor and leaves us a revocable, term-limited licence.
- **Foreign forum.** § 28.1 imposes Singapore law and exclusive Singapore jurisdiction, contradicting the exclusive New York County venue already agreed in § 28.2.

A cluster of Customer-side restraints (§ 2.1 take-or-pay, § 7.2 MFN/match, § 12.4 non-compete, § 12.4 non-solicit/no-hire) each fails the fallback on every material term **and** contradicts § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume or no-hire commitment. Removing them cures the internal inconsistency as well as the commercial exposure. We also have no convenience exit from a three-year term, and no transition-assistance or data-return obligation on exit.

**One item requires attorney review before it is sent:** the § 12.4 non-solicitation redline failed automated verification and is marked *needs review* below.

---

## 2. Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Position / action |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Missing | No indemnity clause; nearest text § 19.5 | Insert new Section 20: Vendor indemnity, claim procedure, and narrow Customer indemnity |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 14.2 | Reverse Deliverable ownership so Customer owns and Vendor assigns each Deliverable |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Compliant | § 21.1 (with §§ 21.2, 21.3) | Preferred position met; no redline |
| High | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | § 28.1 | Replace Singapore law/jurisdiction with New York law; leave § 28.2 New York County venue to operate |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Deviation | § 12.4 (non-compete instance) | Strike the restriction; section marked intentionally omitted (redline auto-repaired — confirm on review) |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | § 2.1 (with §§ 8.1, 9.1–9.3) | Add Customer 30-day convenience right as new § 9.4; bar Vendor convenience termination; conform § 2.1 |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24.1 (with §§ 24.2, 24.4) | Preferred position met; no redline |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § 12.3 | No exclusivity imposed on Customer; no redline |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Compliant | § 27.3 (with §§ 7.1–7.5, 22.2) | No Customer-payable penalty or termination fee; no redline |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 13.1 (with §§ 13.2, 13.3) | Above fallback; no redline |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation burdening Customer | Deviation | § 7.2 | Remove the Customer-side MFN/disclose-and-match obligation |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Deviation | § 2.1 | Delete the three-year take-or-pay minimum; fees payable only for usage or ordered Services |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | **Needs review** | § 12.4 (non-solicit instance) | Remove one-sided non-solicit/no-hire; **verification failed — manual review required before sending** |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Missing | § 10.1 (with §§ 16.5, 15) | Insert new § 10.3: transition assistance and Customer Data return/deletion |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 22.1 (with §§ 22.2, 22.3) | Preferred position met; no redline |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | § 8.2 (with § 8.3) | Preferred position met, including CPI/3% uplift cap; no redline |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § 19.1 (with §§ 19.2–19.5) | Preferred position met on material terms; no redline |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18.1 (with § 18.2) | Preferred position met or exceeded; no redline |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

The following sit in walk-away territory under the playbook and should be treated as conditions to signature, not trading chips:

1. **No Vendor IP indemnity at all** (absent Section 20; presupposed by §§ 9.3, 19.4, 19.5, 21.3, 30.5).
2. **Singapore governing law and exclusive Singapore jurisdiction** (§ 28.1) — outside the accepted forum list and inconsistent with § 28.2.
3. **Non-compete on Customer for the term plus 24 months, undefined scope, any territory** (§ 12.4).
4. **Non-solicit/no-hire on Customer for the term plus 24 months, all Vendor employees, no general-advertisement carve-out** (§ 12.4).
5. **Open-ended Customer-side MFN/disclose-and-match obligation** (§ 7.2) — no defined product, no time limit, no like-for-like carve-outs.
6. **USD 2,000,000/year take-or-pay for three years "without reduction or termination rights"** (§ 2.1).
7. **No Customer termination for convenience in a three-year term**, with § 2.1 expressly denying any reduction or termination right.

Items 3–6 each contradict § 12.3, which we should preserve and cite in negotiation.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Attorney review of the § 12.4 non-solicitation redline** (verification failed) before the markup is released; the § 12.4 non-compete redline was auto-repaired and should also be eyeballed.
2. **Issue the markup** covering the eight actionable items: new Section 20 (indemnity), § 14.2 (Deliverable ownership), § 28.1 (New York law), new § 9.4 plus conforming § 2.1 (convenience termination), § 2.1 (take-or-pay deletion), § 7.2 (MFN deletion), § 12.4 (non-compete and non-solicit), and new § 10.3 (transition and data return).
3. **Flag the § 20.5 cross-reference in § 9.3**, which is currently unmatched. We can align the new Section 20 numbering or add procure/modify/replace/refund remedies if Vendor prefers.
4. **Point Vendor to the internal conflicts** with § 12.3 (and § 7.1's Order Form fee construct) when defending the deletions at §§ 2.1, 7.2 and 12.4 — these are consistency fixes as much as commercial asks.
5. **Hold the compliant clauses as-is**, and resist reopening §§ 13, 18, 19, 21, 22, 24 and 8.2–8.3, which already sit at or above our preferred position.
6. **Confirm business alignment** on the loss of the take-or-pay volume commitment if it was priced into the current discount, and on the transition period we want reflected in new § 10.3."}
